web_evidence.title: Excerpt from The Historian by Elizabeth Kostova
web_evidence.note: A copyright-authorized multi-page opening has the unnamed daughter retrospectively narrate her own life as I; it also embeds Rossi's first-person letter.

web_evidence.title: Campus Novels in an Age of the Global Campus: The Historian by Elizabeth Kostova
web_evidence.note: The scholarly article identifies the woman historian as the retrospective storyteller, analyzes her personal first-person account and nested correspondence, and shows that the closing third-person historical tableau is her brief imaginative reconstruction.

web_evidence.title: Biting Back: A Feminist Analysis of Dracula and The Historian
web_evidence.note: This university honors thesis describes the novel as an epistolary account composed primarily of the narrator's and her father's letters and diary material, with the older participating narrator telling her personal story.

web_evidence.title: Vampires Are Forever: The Historian by Elizabeth Kostova and Dracula by Bram Stoker
web_evidence.note: The review explicitly calls the daughter an unnamed first-person narrator, describes the whole novel as her account, and says journals and letters constitute most of it.

web_evidence.title: The Epistolary Form in Bram Stoker's Dracula and Elizabeth Kostova's The Historian
web_evidence.note: The thesis calls the daughter's narration primarily first person and documents the framed letters, diary, and indirect reconstructions. It mentions third-person shifts when she reconstructs Paul and Rossi but does not establish autonomous sustained third-person sections.

person_note: The controlling account is the unnamed daughter-historian's retrospective story of events she personally experienced, narrated as I. Paul and Rossi contribute extensive first-person letters, diary-like material, and oral accounts; because these documents constitute the layered novel and remain first person, multiple narrators do not make it ALTERNATING. The quote set repeatedly corroborates participating first-person narration. Bare he-sentences such as q01302 occur within a first-person document and are therefore unmarked rather than third-person evidence. Scholarly research notes occasional third-person reconstruction, including a brief imagined historical tableau at the end, but does not show a sustained autonomous third-person narrative section. The remaining uncertainty is only the precise extent of these local reconstructions, not the controlling first-person form.
